angle_title: Dil Kaybı: Hangi Atasözleri Ortadan Kayboluyor?

research_plan.B1_objective: Türkic dillerin yok oluşu ile atasözleri kaybının ilişkisini araştırma planı
target_claims: Dil ölümü hızı: Her 2 haftada/40 günde bir dil
Tuvan, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uyghur atasözleri belgeleme projeleri
Dil ölümü = Atasözleri/sözlü gelenek kaybı ilişkisi
Wikitongues ve benzer kuruluşlar documentation efforts
research_channels: Web: UNESCO, language extinction, endangered Turkic languages
Academic: JSTOR, ResearchGate, academia.edu, Nature journals
Archives: Ethnologue, Glottolog, Endangered Languages Catalogue
Multilingual: Tuvan, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uyghur proverb documentation
Organizations: Wikitongues, Endangered Languages Documentation Programme
research_plan.methodology: Claim decomposition → multi-channel source gathering → adversarial verification

evidence.source_title: UNESCO: 15 Languages Endangered in Turkey
evidence.quote: According to the Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger published by UNESCO, 15 languages are endangered in Turkey

language_details.languages: Abaza, Homshetsma, Laz, Pontus Greek, Romani, Suret, Western Armenian

evidence.cause: Decades of government policies not putting other languages on equal footing with Turkish (80% of population)

evidence.source_title: Turkey's Endangered Languages
Lost words: The struggle to save Turkey's disappearing languages

claims_and_evidence.claim_text: Her iki haftada bir dil yok oluyor (One language dies every two weeks)

evidence.source_title: New Estimates on the Rate of Global Language Loss
evidence.finding: The frequently-cited 'one language every two weeks' claim appears inaccurate
evidence.correction: ELCat (Endangered Languages Catalogue) finds ~3.5 languages extinct per year = about 1 every 4 months, not 2 weeks

evidence.source_title: Dying Language Statistics 2026
evidence.finding: A language dies off every 40 days
evidence.calculation: 365 days / 40 = ~9 languages per year (roughly similar to ELCat finding)

evidence.source_title: Language Vitality and Endangerment UNESCO
evidence.finding: Levels of language loss could triple in next 40 years with at least one language per month disappearing unless measures taken

claims_and_evidence.analysis: The 'one language every two weeks' is a popular figure but has been disputed by ELCat. Current rate appears closer to one language every 40 days (9-10 per year) or one per 3-4 months.

claims_and_evidence.claim_text: 2100'de 50-90% diller tehlikeli/ölü olacak (50-90% of languages endangered/dead by 2100)

evidence.source_title: This is why half of the world's languages are endangered
evidence.finding: Earlier estimates lead to prospects of death of 50-90% of world's languages by end of century

evidence.source_title: The World's Most Endangered Languages in 2026
evidence.finding: At current transmission rates, 90% of world's languages could disappear by 2100

claims_and_evidence.analysis: 2100 projection is widely cited and relatively consistent across sources: 50-90% language loss.

claims_and_evidence.claim_text: Günümüzde dünya dillerinin 43%'ü tehlikede (Currently 43% of world's languages endangered)

evidence.source_title: The World's Most Endangered Languages in 2026
evidence.finding: Of the 7,168 languages spoken on Earth today, 3,078 (43%) are classified as endangered
evidence.additional_stats: 1,431 languages have fewer than 1,000 first-language speakers

evidence.source_title: Global predictors of language endangerment and the future of linguistic diversity

claims_and_evidence.claim_text: Dil ölümü = Atasözleri/sözlü gelenek kaybı (Language death directly correlates with proverb and oral tradition loss)

evidence.source_title: The Consequences of Losing a Minority Language: Cultural Erosion and Beyond
evidence.finding: When a language dies, the culture it embodies often fades with it, including traditional practices, folklore, and ways of life unique to that linguistic community

evidence.source_title: Disappearing Oral Proverbs and Storytelling Traditions
evidence.finding: Many minority languages contain wealth of oral tradition with stories, songs, proverbs passed down through generations preserving local knowledge

evidence.source_title: Knowledge is power: anthropology of proverbs
evidence.finding: Proverbs as ethnographic and anthropological data source for cultural memory and transmission

evidence.source_title: Oral Traditions and Expressions
evidence.finding: UNESCO recognizes oral traditions (including proverbs) as Intangible Cultural Heritage endangered by language death

evidence.source_title: The Role of Proverbs in Language Learning
evidence.finding: Proverbs as cognitive and cultural resources deeply embedded in native language idioms/rhythm/metaphor that resist translation

claims_and_evidence.analysis: The connection between language death and proverb loss is well-established in linguistic anthropology and UNESCO documentation.
